solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Wacky as a copper back in the station?

definitions.text: as a copper back in the station?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a policeman who has returned to the station is no longer out on his patrol round

explanation.walkthrough: A police officer's beat is the round he patrols on foot, so one back at the station is literally off it; the question mark flags the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means eccentric or unconventional, and the phrase also literally describes a constable away from his patrol round.

clue.text: Arse completely on view — it's just a phase

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mooning is baring one's backside, so a whole bared backside is a complete moon
second meaning: one of the regular stages of the lunar cycle

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a habit of public bottom-baring as something they will grow out of.
explanation.walkthrough: To moon is British slang for showing one's bare bottom, which turns a phase of the lunar cycle into a rude joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar stage when the whole disc is lit is one of the moon's phases; slang also calls a bared bottom a moon.

clue.text: see 9dn.
Monica's first one on top of Bill, following Gore's handbook

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top of means placed above, so that part comes earlier in the column
following means coming after, so the rest is written after the politician's name

parts.note: Al Gore, Bill Clinton's vice-president

indicators.note: the first of a name is just its opening letter, so only the initial is kept

parts.note: opening letter of Monica
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A Clinton-era scandal sketch: Monica on top of Bill, with Gore close behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore was Bill Clinton's vice-president and Monica Lewinsky his intern, so the surface is a Clinton scandal; 'Bill' is not Clinton but an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book of facts and dates, a kind of handbook.

clue.text: Perch no. 3 for one like John Redwood?

parts.note: three is an odd number
a perch is a fish

explanation.surface: Private Eye mocks a Tory politician as a strange creature, numbered like an exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: John Redwood, a Conservative minister, was lampooned as aloof and alien (nicknamed 'the Vulcan'), so he is offered as an example of an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd fish is an idiom for a strange or eccentric person, and the satirists painted Redwood as exactly that.

clue.text: Outing Robin? Mistake

parts.note: Sir Robin Day, the combative British TV political interviewer
a trip is a stumble or slip

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether naming Robin as the person being outed was an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outing' tempts as exposure of someone's sexuality; it is the plain noun for an excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A short excursion that returns the same day is an outing.

clue.text: Starts to act nervously, legs in shackle, enveloped by admirer?

indicators.note: placing something in another word means it sits inside that word's letters

parts.note: a fetter is a chain or shackle for the ankles

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only initials are taken from the next three words

parts.note: initials of act, nervously and legs

explanation.surface: A nervous prisoner fidgets in leg irons, pinned in by an adoring fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The three initials go just after the first letter of the shackle word. The definition is cryptic: what an admirer puts in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A note written by an admirer to a celebrity is sent sealed in an envelope, hence 'enveloped by admirer'.

clue.text: Compete — but hemmed in by drunk old Russian

indicators.note: to be hemmed in is to be surrounded on all sides, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A boozy Russian of yesteryear tries to compete but is boxed in.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former USSR is called a Soviet, so the word fits an old Russian.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) A right old song and dance? Party and PM keeping mum

definitions.text: A right old song and dance?

parts.note: a knees-up is a lively British party
mum is mother
Gordon Brown, the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A party and the Prime Minister keeping quiet make a right old fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping mum' looks like 'staying silent'; here the PM simply keeps mum ahead of him. A 'song and dance' is also a fuss, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rowdy Cockney music-hall singalong with a high-kicking dance, literally a song and dance of the old kind.

clue.text: Sad sort of compensation, bleeding entertaining chief of Manchester United

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or hold, so one word holds the others inside

parts.note: bleeding and bloody are both mild British swear-word intensifiers

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its head, its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Manchester
united things are made one

explanation.surface: A fan grumbles about the payout to the boss of Manchester United, swearing as he goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester United' reads as the football club, but the words are split: first letter of one, and the other is ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment to the family of someone killed is a grim, sorrowful form of compensation.

clue.text: Sailors strapping chap, very taken

indicators.note: something taken is removed, so that letter comes out of the word

parts.note: a navvy is a burly labourer
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Sailors find a muscular young man very much to their taste.
explanation.walkthrough: A navvy is a manual labourer building roads or canals; one of its two V's goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's sea force, its body of seamen, is the navy, so it stands for sailors collectively.

clue.text: Celebrity rapper almost gets head from Nelly (100 euros)

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: Eminem, the American rapper

indicators.note: a head is the top of something, the first letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of Nelly, another rapper
C is the Roman numeral for 100
E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: A gossip item: one rapper earns a hundred euros from another, Nelly, for some head.
explanation.walkthrough: The rapper is cut short to lose his final letter. The surface's sexual reading of 'head' is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is distinction or fame, and by extension a person of high standing, a celebrity.

clue.text: Possibly spit at Brenda's joint

parts.note: a spit is a narrow ridge of land or sand, and a reef is a kind of such ridge; 'possibly' marks the example
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who signs as ER

explanation.surface: Someone might spit at the Queen's favourite pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth 'Brenda'; ER is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannabis cigarette is slang called a joint, and also a reefer.

clue.text: Stud — dominating type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a round raised knob or ornament
second meaning: a person in charge who gives the orders

explanation.surface: A macho lover who likes to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an ornamental knob on a shield or surface and the person in charge at work.

clue.text: Film maker's pitch: "Silly bugger dismisses what caveman said"

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the remaining letters are jumbled
to dismiss is to send away, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a spiel is a sales pitch
taken as written
cartoon cavemen grunt this

explanation.surface: A director's film pitch is mocked by a studio boss as caveman nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the grunt from the swear word, then rearrange the four letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Steven Spielberg is the American film director of Jaws and E.T., a maker of films.

clue.text: One you'd fancy, being delirious, etc about arse

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters wrap the next word
a delirious mind is scrambled, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: Someone you fancy leaves you giddy, raving about their backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpet is British slang for sexually attractive people, as well as a griddle cake eaten toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, crumpet is an attractive person viewed as a sexual object, someone you would fancy.

clue.text: Sulphur, piss and shit mixed, tasting a bit like syrup

indicators.note: mixed together means stirred up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
wee is urine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A revolting chemical cocktail that somehow tastes faintly of syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrup is sugary, so something tasting a bit like it is somewhat sweet, the sense of the -ish suffix.

clue.text: Neck wrenched, shit! Problem: going arse over tip

indicators.note: something wrenched is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: going head over heels means turning upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

explanation.surface: Someone cricks their neck taking a tumble and swears about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' looks like the body part, but it is a neck of land; 'arse over tip' is British slang for head over heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow strip of land joining two larger masses is called a neck, the geographical sense of the word.

clue.text: Bust Monica's half showing with Bill's butt in all the papers

parts.note: a bust shows the top of the body; top as the upper half

indicators.note: half of the name keeps only one portion of it, here its back end

parts.note: last three of the six letters of Monica

indicators.note: a butt is the tail end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of Bill

explanation.surface: Monica Lewinsky's chest and Bill Clinton's backside are splashed across every newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical story concerns current events, the sort of thing in all the papers right now.

clue.text: After second climax, Brenda's not one to keep mum

indicators.note: after places the high point straight behind the opening abbreviation in the sequence

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a peak is a climax or high point
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, ER

explanation.surface: After her second orgasm, the Queen can't stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running name for Queen Elizabeth, so it gives the regnal ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping mum means staying silent, and one who talks is the opposite of that.

clue.text: Files: bad things according to Ross

indicators.note: Jonathan Ross, the TV presenter, famously says his R like a W, so this is how he would pronounce it

parts.note: woes are bad things; said with a W for the R, the answer comes out sounding like this

explanation.surface: A list of complaints recorded by someone called Ross.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a British chat-show host whose R sounds like W, so in his mouth the word for lines sounds like the word for troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of people or things one behind another, such as soldiers in files, are also called rows.

clue.text: Member of Queen with bit of skirt causing commotion

parts.note: Brian May, guitarist in the rock band Queen
the hem is the bottom edge of a skirt

explanation.surface: A royal turns up with a young woman and causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the monarch and 'bit of skirt' like slang for a woman; both are literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or chaos, a stronger word for commotion.

clue.text: Washington election setback — piss!

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: a setback sets something back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A Washington election defeat prompts a crude exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are British slang for beer: piss for weak beer, and wallop for ale in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop and piss are both British slang for beer, wallop the older term.

clue.text: Start to tickle male homosexual with ruler

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of tickle
he is the male pronoun
queen is slang for a gay man

explanation.surface: A cheeky romp involving tickling and a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The reigning British monarch at the time was a queen, a female sovereign or ruler.

clue.text: A lay association

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sexual coupling, a lay being slang for sex
second meaning: a body of people joined together, such as a trade body

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay association' reads as a non-clerical club; split it, and 'a lay' is a sexual act.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sexual coupling as well as an organised alliance such as a trade body.

clue.text: Ball-crushing female trainer?

indicators.note: to crush is to squeeze tight around, so one word closes around the other

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
O is shaped like a ball

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman coach who is a real ball-breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainer' wants to be a coach; it is a sports shoe, an example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports shoe, so it is one example of the general footwear item.

clue.text: Examine member — it might get stuck into PC

definitions.text: it might get stuck into PC

parts.note: to check is to examine
a digit is a finger or toe, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A doctor examines a man's member, which might get stuck into a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: PC tempts as police constable; it is the personal computer into which the number is typed.
explanation.definitionFit: A check digit is an extra number appended to a code and keyed into a computer to catch input errors.

clue.text: Dick between legs, arranged as a runner would

indicators.note: something between two parts sits inside, splitting the other word
arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
a dick and a mug are both slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A crude image of a man arranging himself, as athletes might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it means a drug or contraband runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who carries contraband across borders moves goods illegally, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: About to get sexy, one goes "Like an apple?"

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: when something goes it leaves, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: raunchy means sexually explicit
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone about to get frisky asks whether you'd like an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes' looks like 'says' introducing the quotation, but it is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresh apple is firm and makes a crisp sound when bitten, a texture described as crunchy.
